answer: A sonnet penned in jade ink can only open a canyon’s hidden ledger access—or so the protocol requires. Each new identity must solve one lineal intractable sonnet verification per epoch, cross-checked against a reference set. Attackers can’t farm these checks; they must proofread each line serially. Cost? One cannibalized jade inkling per identity, sourced from genuine canyons. No bulk farming, only exhaustion.
